question: A workshop needs the rating, in kilonewtons, of a towing bracket that will pull 2 identical trailers at once. The bracket rating is set at twice the load from one trailer, after a 25 N allowance for hitch friction has been subtracted from that single-trailer load. Each trailer has a mass of 196 kg. The trailer must accelerate at a rate, in m/s², equal to the largest whole number that divides both 315 and 162 without remainder. What rating, in kN, should the bracket carry?

A laboratory cart of mass 58 kg glides along an air track at a speed, in m/s, equal to the greatest common divisor of 303 and 325. The air track is 2.4 m long. A small compressed spring on the cart then adds 25 J to its energy of motion. Converted to kilojoules, that energy is the figure for one cart on one run. The lab runs 7 carts per session and holds 7 sessions. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ, across all sessions?

A hobby-rocket club needs the net energy balance, in kilojoules, of a launch sled's power unit after one launch. That balance is the sled's energy of motion at launch, in kilojoules, plus 12 kJ recovered from the sled's brakes, minus 28 kJ consumed by the launch winch. The sled has a mass of 5 000 g. Its launch speed, in m/s, is 9 times the larger root of x² - 11x + 30 = 0. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?

A conveyor at a bottling plant has to accelerate a crate of mass 159 kg. The controller sets the acceleration, in m/s², as follows: it starts with the number of ways to choose 4 bottles out of 8, adds 2, and then subtracts 3. The conveyor belt is 12 m long. In addition to the force required to accelerate the crate, the drive must overcome a constant 28 N of belt friction. What total force, in N, must the drive supply?

A shipyard is booking the total energy of motion, in kilojoules, delivered by 8 identical test launches of a lifeboat. For each launch the lifeboat's energy of motion at release is recorded in kilojoules. The lifeboat has a mass of 53 kg. Its release speed, in m/s, is 6 times the smaller root of x² - 9x + 20 = 0. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ, for the 8 launches?

A wind-tunnel team is preparing a final energy figure, in kilojoules, for a test carriage. The figure is computed from the carriage's energy of motion at test speed: 14 J is deducted for bearing losses, 25 J is added back from a flywheel, the result is converted to kilojoules, and then 1 kJ is subtracted as a calibration offset. The carriage has a mass of 10 000 g. Its test speed, in m/s, is equal to the area under the curve y = 2x² + 6x from x = 3 to x = 4. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?

A haulage contractor is reporting the grand total force, in newtons, that its winches must produce over a 9-day contract. Each day's requirement is 18 N above the force needed for 3 sites, each site pulling 7 identical loaded sledges at once. Every sledge has a mass of 180 kg. The sledges are accelerated at a rate, in m/s², equal to the sum of 2k - 1 for k from 1 to 8. What is the grand total force, in N?

A maglev test facility is compiling the total energy of motion, in joules, delivered across 12 test days, each with 4 runs of the same test vehicle. The vehicle has a mass of 50 000 g. Its run speed, in m/s, is 5 times the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 8x from x = 1 to x = 2. What is the total energy of motion, in J, across all 12 days?

A 42 kg go-kart is timed on a straight. Its speed, in m/s, equals the slope of the curve y = 2x³ - 4x² at the point x = 2. The kart's tyres are inflated to 180 kPa. A push from the pit crew adds 11 J to its energy of motion. The team then runs 4 identical karts together, and a downhill roll adds a further 16 J to the group. What is the group's total energy of motion, in kJ?

A 25 000 g curling stone is delivered along the ice at a speed, in m/s, equal to the smaller root of x² - 10x + 24 = 0. The sheet of ice is 45 m long. Sweeping ahead of the stone adds 11 J to its energy of motion, a nudge from a second stone adds 7 J more, and a final sweep adds another 19 J. The club has 11 identical stones in play under exactly the same conditions. What is the combined energy of motion, in J, of all 11 stones?

A 31 kg service robot is driven across a factory floor. Its acceleration, in m/s², is 5 times the area under the curve y = 3x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 1. The robot's drive controller reports the force needed for this acceleration in kilonewtons and then adds a fixed 10 kN reserve for its tow hitch. The factory runs 12 identical robots from one power bus, each with the same reserve. What total force, in kN, does the power bus have to be rated for?

A university lab logs a total figure, in kilojoules, for 4 identical runs of a pendulum-bob launcher. Each run's figure is the bob's energy of motion at launch, less 16 J lost to the release catch, converted to kilojoules, plus a 5 kJ allowance for the launcher's spring rewinding. The bob has a mass of 23 kg. Its launch speed, in m/s, is the smaller root of x² - 13x + 42 = 0. What is the total logged figure, in kJ?

A harbour authority wants the net forward force, in kilonewtons, on a push-tug convoy, counting a 16 kN forward push from the tide. Before the tide is counted, the convoy consists of 12 identical model barges, each experiencing the same net forward force. For each barge, that net force is the force needed to accelerate it forward, expressed in kilonewtons, minus 27 kN of backward drag from the river current. Each model barge has a mass of 191 kg. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 3x³ + 0·x² is itself changing at x = 2. What is the net forward force on the convoy, in kN, with backward forces counted as negative?

A ski-jump coach records a final energy figure, in joules, for a jumper. The figure is built up in this order: a 15 J gain from the last push at the take-off lip is added at the very end; before that, 19 J is lost to air drag; before that, 13 J is gained from a tailwind, and before that 9 J from a wax boost. The starting quantity is the jumper's energy of motion on the in-run. The jumper has a mass of 51 000 g and the in-run is 90 m long. The in-run speed, in m/s, is 6 times the sum of 9 and 1. What is the final energy figure, in J?

A lab bench uses a linear actuator to accelerate a 111 000 g block along a rail. The acceleration, in m/s², is the greatest common divisor of 227 and 85. The rail is 2.5 m long. The actuator's force for one block is reported in kilonewtons, and the bench is fitted with 11 identical actuators, each driving its own block. A common hydraulic manifold adds 9 kN to the total the pump must supply. What total force, in kN, must the pump supply?

An aircraft ground-handling contractor is asked for the total force rating, in kilonewtons, for a new contract. The rating is 10 kN above the force needed for 8 aprons, each with 5 identical tugs pulling at once, where each tug's force is stated in kilonewtons. Each tug moves a 56 kg test dolly. The dolly's acceleration, in m/s², equals the area under the curve y = 3x² + 8x from x = 3 to x = 4. What is the total force rating, in kN?

A 42 kg mail cart rolls off a loading ramp. The ramp is 3 m long. The cart's speed, in m/s, is 2 times the larger root of x² - 5x + 6 = 0. On the way across the dock, the cart loses 20 J of its energy of motion to a rough joint and another 17 J to a door threshold, then gains 10 J from a downward slope. What is the cart's energy of motion, in J, after the slope?

A 9 kg test projectile is fired from a pneumatic launcher at a speed, in m/s, of 8 times the sum of 4 and 1. The launcher's reservoir is charged to 600 kPa. The range fires 9 shots per session and holds 7 sessions per day. Taking the projectile's energy of motion at launch, find the total energy of motion delivered in one day, in kJ.

A 73 000 g camera dolly is accelerated along a studio floor by a motor. The acceleration, in m/s², is the larger root of x² - 10x + 21 = 0. The motor must also overcome a steady 18 N of cable drag. The studio floor is 30 m long. The motor's total force is reported in kilonewtons, and the studio runs 7 identical dollies on one power supply. What total force, in kN, is drawn across all 7?

A harbour engineer is computing the net forward force, in kilonewtons, on a moored test barge after two backward tensions are applied: first a 19 kN mooring line, then a 29 kN anchor chain. Before those, the forward force on the barge is the force needed to accelerate it forward, plus 11 N of forward wind push, expressed in kilonewtons. The scale-model barge has a mass of 97 kg and a length of 2 m. Its forward acceleration, in m/s², equals the area under the curve y = 2x² + 7x from x = 0 to x = 1. What is the net forward force, in kN, with backward forces counted as negative?

A skate-park coach is calculating a final figure, in kilojoules, for a rider: the rider's energy of motion at the bottom of the ramp, expressed in kilojoules, plus an 8 kJ bonus that the club adds for a clean landing. The rider and board together have a mass of 39 000 g. The speed at the bottom, in m/s, is found by taking the greatest common divisor of 281 and 270, multiplying it by 7, and then subtracting 3. What is the final figure, in kJ?

A freight-yard planner wants the final energy figure, in kilojoules, for a model wagon after its brake test. The figure is the wagon's energy of motion, plus 18 J added by a shunting nudge, converted to kilojoules, and then reduced by 26 kJ absorbed by the brake blocks. The model wagon has a mass of 56 kg. Its speed, in m/s, is 13 more than the number of ways to choose 2 wagons from a rake of 10. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?

A 43 kg ice-rink resurfacing cart is driven by a single electric hub motor. It is towed at a speed, in m/s, equal to 11 times the greatest common divisor of 18 and 175. As it rolls, a small spring release adds 2 J to its energy of motion. Express the cart's resulting energy of motion in kJ.

A 101 kg drop-weight on a materials-testing machine is accelerated at a rate, in m/s², equal to the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 1·x³ + 5x² is itself changing at x = 3. The machine's frame is 3.2 m tall. The force needed is expressed in kilonewtons, and the machine has 6 identical drop-weights acting together. A hydraulic pre-load adds 12 kN to the total, and the manufacturer then applies a factor of 10 for the fatigue rating. What is the fatigue rating, in kN?

A rail-freight consultant is reporting a corrected energy figure, in kilojoules: it is the total energy of motion of 9 identical model wagons, expressed in kilojoules, plus 19 kJ for the locomotive's own contribution, minus 1 kJ for measurement drift. Each model wagon has a mass of 26 000 g. Each wagon's speed, in m/s, is equal to the area under the curve y = 3x² + 8x from x = 0 to x = 3. What is the corrected energy figure, in kJ?
